questions.ask: Where do your bookings, orders or client records live today?

options.saas_with_api: In an online service (booking system, CRM, shop platform)
options.mostly_offline: Mostly on paper, phone and memory

questions.ask: How do customers reach you today?

saas_with_api.note: Your system already speaks API: the standard build path, live in about two weeks of scoped work.

spreadsheets_calendars.note: Spreadsheets and calendars are workable sources: we bridge them, and the connector becomes the tidy front.

custom_software.note: Custom software with any kind of API is our home ground: the connector is built against your endpoints.

mostly_offline.note: Before a connector helps, bookings need a digital home. The scoping call maps the smallest system that gives you one.

channelNotes.phone_messengers: When inquiries live in calls and DMs, your team repeats the same answers all day: the connector moves availability checks, bookings and the repeat questions into the chat.
channelNotes.website_forms: You already collect structured requests: the connector turns form-and-wait into an instant answer-and-confirm inside the chat.
channelNotes.walk_in: In person is where the real work happens, and everything before it still costs you time: the chat answers the hours, prices and availability questions, and books the visit before anyone arrives.
channelNotes.mixed: Scattered channels mean lost context and double answers: the connector gives every inbox the same live schedule and records to work from.

verticals.title: Clinics and medical practices
customers: **Find and book the right appointment.** "I need a check-up with a hygienist in the next two weeks, mornings only": the assistant matches practitioner, appointment type and your real availability.
**Get practical answers before coming in**: what to bring, how long the visit takes, how preparation works, which insurers you work with. All from your own practice information.
**Reschedule or cancel** a booked visit, within your notice rules.
**Ask what a procedure involves** in plain language, from text your practitioners approved.
**Handle the paperwork trail**: request a referral, ask for a receipt or a document. The request routes to the right person at your practice.
team: **Open the day in one question.** Tomorrow's list per practitioner and per room, read from your scheduling system.
**See what needs chasing**: unconfirmed appointments, overnight cancellations, reschedule requests waiting for an answer.
**Pull the administrative context before a call**: visit history, documents requested, insurer on file.
**Adjust the schedule from the chat**: move an appointment, block a slot, mark a no-show. Each change confirmed before it fires.

verticals.title: Online shops and e-commerce
customers: **Find a product by describing it**, not by guessing your search keywords: "a waterproof jacket for cycling, under a hundred, in stock in medium".
**Check real stock and delivery dates** for a specific variant, instead of a generic shipping page.
**Ask the questions that block a purchase**: sizing, materials, care, compatibility. Answered from your product data and policies.
**Track an order**: "where is my parcel?" answered from your fulfilment system rather than from imagination.
**Start a return or exchange** and get told exactly what your policy allows.
**Reorder a consumable** they have bought before.
team: **See what needs attention**: orders unfulfilled past your own threshold, deliveries running late, returns waiting for a decision.
**Answer a support message with the facts open**: the customer's orders, delivery state and return history in one question, before typing a reply.
**Check stock the way you actually think about it**: "what is running low in the winter line", across variants, from the same catalog API.
**Get the day in one digest**: what sold, what came back, what got stuck. Numbers read from your systems, not estimated.

verticals.title: Local and on-site services
customers: **Describe the problem and get a real next step.** "My boiler is making a knocking noise, can someone come this week?": the assistant asks the qualifying questions your intake form asks, then offers genuine visit slots.
**Check whether you cover their address** and what the callout terms are for it, before anyone's time is spent.
**Book a visit window** that matches your dispatch reality: the crew, the travel time, the equipment.
**Ask for an indicative estimate** from your own price list, framed exactly as your business frames it: a range and its conditions, never a number the model made up.
**Track a job**: when is the technician coming, what happened on the last visit, is the part in.
team: **Open the morning in one question.** Today's jobs, who is assigned where, which visit windows are tight.
**See what is unassigned**: jobs without a crew, gaps in this week's schedule worth filling.
**Pull the job context before knocking**: what the customer reported, what happened on the last visit, whether the part arrived.
**Update a job from the road**: move a visit window, log an outcome, flag a follow-up. Each change confirmed before it fires.

verticals.title: Private education and tutoring
customers: **Book a trial lesson in one sentence.** "My daughter is 9, we want to try English on weekday evenings": the assistant matches level, group and your real schedule, and confirms a trial.
**Move a lesson without the guilt call.** A sick child at 7am becomes a reschedule inside the chat, within your notice rules.

**Ask what a program actually involves**: levels, group sizes, how long until results, what the difference between two courses is. Answered from your own program descriptions, not from the model's imagination.
**Keep the money side clear**: what is paid, how many lessons are left on the package, when the next payment is due, with payment by a secure link.
**Enroll the second child or renew a package** as a confirmed action, not a form hunt.
team: **Open the day in one question.** Today's groups, rooms and teachers, read from your schedule, not from a whiteboard photo.
**See what needs a call**: trials that did not convert, packages ending this month, absences piling up for one student.
**Pull the context before talking to a parent**: attendance, progress notes, payment state. Instead of asking a colleague who remembers.
**Adjust the schedule from the chat**: move a lesson, mark an absence, block a room. Each change confirmed before it fires.

verticals.title: Professional services and agencies
customers: **Ask "where are we?" and get a real answer.** Project status, what shipped this week, what is waiting on their side. All read from your project tracker, not from a manager's memory.
**Book a call with the right person**: their account manager, not a generic inbox, against the team's real availability.
**Check the money side without an awkward email**: what the retainer covers, which invoices are open, when the next one lands.
**Hand over what you are waiting for.** The assistant tells them exactly which access, file or approval is blocking work, and confirms when it is in.
**Ask what a service involves**: timelines, what is in scope and what is not. Answered from your own service descriptions, framed the way you frame them.
team: **Open the week in one question.** Active projects, deadlines this week, which clients have not heard from you lately.
**See what needs attention across tools**: stale proposals in the CRM, unbilled work in the tracker, invoices overdue in the books. One answer instead of three tabs.
**Pull the client context before a call**: history, open items, last invoices, who promised what. Instead of scrolling three threads.
**Log the outcome from the chat**: a follow-up task, a note on the account, a nudge to billing. Each change confirmed before it fires.

verticals.title: Restaurants, cafés and bars
customers: **Reserve a table** by describing the occasion: "a table for four on Friday around eight, somewhere quiet". The assistant reads your real availability and confirms.

**Ask the menu real questions.** What is gluten-free tonight, what changed on the seasonal menu, what goes with a dish. Answered from your actual menu data, with allergens straight from your source of truth rather than guessed.
**Order for pickup or delivery**, where your ordering system supports it, without leaving the conversation.
**Handle the group logistics**: change the party size, note a birthday, add a high chair. The details that usually cost a phone call.
**Find out what is on**: set menus, tastings, live music. All from your events data.
team: **Open the service in one question.** Tonight's covers, the large parties, the notes that matter: birthdays, high chairs, allergies guests flagged.
**See the load per seating**: which slots are full, which tables are still free, where a walk-in could fit.
**Catch the overnight changes**: cancellations, shrunk parties, no-shows worth a follow-up.
**Adjust the book from the chat**: hold a table, move a reservation, close a slot. Each change confirmed before it fires.

verticals.title: SaaS products and customer support
customers: **Get answers grounded in your documentation**, with the source attached, so a user can check what they were told instead of trusting a paraphrase.
**Ask about their own account**: which plan, what usage this month, when the renewal falls, why an invoice looks the way it does.
**Do the routine account jobs**: invite a teammate, rotate a key, change a notification setting. All explicit, confirmed actions.
**Open a support ticket** with the context of the conversation already attached, so your team does not start from "hi, what happened?".
**Follow a setup path** step by step, with the assistant checking your API for whether each step actually took effect.
team: **Walk into a call prepared.** One question pulls the account's plan, usage, renewal date and open tickets. Instead of four dashboard tabs.
**Triage the queue with the facts attached**: each new ticket next to the account's actual state, so priority calls are made on data.
**Watch the edges**: which accounts hit their limits this week, whose renewal is coming, who went quiet after an incident.
**Do the routine account jobs for a customer**: resend an invoice, adjust a setting. All explicit, confirmed actions logged to the account.

verticals.title: Salons and beauty studios
customers: **Book an appointment in one sentence.** "Book me a haircut with Marina on Saturday afternoon": the assistant checks who is free, offers the real open times, and confirms one.
**Pick by person, service or time.** A specific stylist, a specific treatment, or simply "the first slot after work this week".
**Reschedule or cancel** without a phone call, inside the same conversation.

**Ask what a service involves**: how long it takes, what to come prepared with, what the difference is between two treatments. Answered from your own service descriptions, not from the model's imagination.
**Rebook what they had last time**, once the connector can see their history.
team: **Open the day in one question.** "Who is booked with whom today?": the schedule, read out from your booking system, not from a printout.
**Spot the money leaks**: which slots are still empty tomorrow, who cancelled overnight, which regulars have not rebooked.
**Check a client before they sit down**: last visit, usual treatment, notes your team left.
**Move the schedule from the chat**: block a slot, shift a booking, mark a no-show. Each change confirmed before it fires.
